column2: Commentary
Instrument Number:

Aker Kvaerner Chemetics standard instrument number is to be used for all projects.  Instrument numbers are taken from the master instrument list for each particular technology.  The owner column is only to be filled in if by contract we must use the Owner's numbering system.  For criteria/basic engineering projects this column should be left blank.
P&ID:
The P&ID which each particular instrument is physically located.
Fluid:
The type of fluid the control valve is actually operating in.  Be specific - use the fluid description given in 1-LST-0002 Fluid Codes.
Composition:

List all major components in the fluid stream in % weight/weight.  % volume/volume can be used for gases.  Trace components should be specified when they potentially have an impact on materials of construction (e.g. trace Cl2 or trace hypo).
Physical Properties at N.O.C
Density, Viscosity and Vapour pressure at normal (flowsheet) temperature, composition and pressure.
Flowrate:
Min. - minimum expected flow through valve during plant operation, turndown, upset, sutdown or start-up conditions.
Norm. - flowsheet value
Max. - maximum expected flow through valve during plant operation, turndown, upset, shutdown or start-up conditions.
Note: All 3 columns must be filled out.
Temperature:
Min. - minimum expected temperature during plant operation, normal turndown, upset, shutdown or start-up conditions.  Consider ambient temperature.
Norm. - flowsheet value
Max. - maximum expected temperature during plant operation, upset, shutdown or start-up conditions.  Consider ambient temperature.
Note:  Maximum temperature is not the pipe or equipment design temperature.  All 3 columns must be filled out.
Inlet Pressure:
Calculated line pressure at valve inlet at each of the minimum, normal and maximum flows.
Not required for criteria/basic engineering projects.
Note: All 3 columns must be filled out.
Pressure Drop:
Calculated pressure drop across the valve at each of the minimum, normal and maximum flows.
Not required for criteria/basic engineering projects.
Note: All 3 columns must be filled out.
Shut-off Pressure:
Maximum expected line pressure at valve inlet.  Consider pump dead head pressure, thermal expansion and relief valve set pressure.
Not required for criteria/basic engineering projects.
Fail Action:
Fail closed (FC), Fail open (FO) or fail last position (FLP)
Continued…
Control Type:

Based on experience and cost, state the recommended type(s) of control valve (e.g. butterfly, ball, globe).  Identify the level of control required for any given application.  i.e., 1 = critical control, 2 = moderate control, 3 = non-critcal control.
Control Loop Accuracy:
Specify 0.5 to 1%, 1% or 2%
Leakage Class:
Class I to III - not normally used.
Class IV - Intended for single -port and balanced single - port valves with extra tight piston seals and metal to metal seats.  Leakage rate is limited to 0.01% of rated valve capacity.

Class V - Intended for same types of valves as class IV.  The test fluid is water at 100 psig or operating pressure.  Leakage rated is limited to 0.0005 l/min of water per mm of port diameter per bar differential.

Class VI - Intended for resilient seating valves.  Test fluid is air or nitrogen.  Pressure is lesser of 50 psig or operating pressure.  Leakage limit is 0.15 to 6.75 ml per min or 2 to 45 bubbles per min. for valve sizes 1 through 8 inches.
Material of Construction
Wetted parts - recommended material(s) for all instrument parts that come into contact with fluid.  Previous project(s) Instrument Spec. can be used as a reference.
Non-wetted parts - Note any special requirements such as paint, plastic, etc. required to protect against environment, spills, leakage, etc. Not required for criteria/basic engineering project.
Gasket/Seal - recommended material(s) for all gaskets, o-rings, etc. (e.g. PTFE, EPDM, Kalrez)
Operating Case Reference:
Reference plant(s) that have used same control valve.
Not required for criteria/basic engineering project.
Comments:

1)  Any additional information that would be helpful in the selection (e.g. Model number, manufacturer, operating experience, included with packaged equipment).
2)  Manually loaded control valves (HV-XXXX) will have rack and pinion type actuators.
3)  If control is the most critical of the min. or max. condition, please specify, e.g., If the control valvve is to only control at the minimum condition and then go wide open during an upset or shutdown, this must be made clear in this column.
4)  If an oversized valve is required, state specific reason.
